cards.definition: A person or thing that does the action named by the word it follows.
Having or showing the quality named by the word it follows.
Without the thing or quality named by the word it follows.
The state or quality of being a certain way.
A very small amount compared with what is needed or with what is already there.
A place with a service or business where information about one person or group is kept.
A feature passed down in a group of living things that helps them survive or have young in a particular place.
A set of clear steps for solving a problem or doing a job.
The set of letters used to write one or more languages. The letters usually have an agreed order.
One of the tiny air sacs in the lungs where gases move between air and blood.
A change or addition made to a formal document, a law, or a proposal.
A channel or pipe built to carry water from one place to another, sometimes across a bridge.
A scientist who studies the people of the past through things they left behind, such as tools, buildings, or pieces of pottery.
A group or chain of islands. It can also mean the area of water that holds them.
A collection of records saved so people can consult them in the future, or the place that keeps them.
The amount of flat space inside a shape.
A small, mostly rocky object that circles the Sun. Many of them travel between Mars and Jupiter.
The layer of gases held around a planet, moon, or star by gravity.
A tiny piece of matter that is still one particular chemical element. Gold is made of gold atoms, for example.
An imaginary or real line around which something turns.
To trade goods or work directly without using money.
A flying mammal with wings made of thin skin stretched over long finger bones.
A muscle at the front of your upper arm that helps bend your elbow.
Using only two choices, like the digits 0 and 1 in computer numbers.
A small piece or amount of something.
A stretchy pouch inside the body that holds urine until you pee.
A line that shows where one area ends and another begins.
A way to read and write using patterns of raised dots that can be felt with the fingers.
To help people feel more comfortable and start talking when they first meet or feel shy.
To carry or guide someone or something to a place or to another person.
To get something by paying money for it.
A group of eight bits that a computer handles as a unit.
The city or town where a country’s or state’s main government is based.
A gas whose molecules each contain one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms. You release some of it when you breathe out.
To stop and hold something that is moving through the air or trying to get away.
A tiny unit that can carry out the basic jobs of life. Living things are made of one or more cells.
An official count of the people who live in a place. The count may also collect other information about them.
A room or an enclosed space inside something.
To ask someone to pay a price for something.
A young person who has not yet grown into an adult.
A green substance in plants and some other living things that absorbs light used to make sugars.
To decide which person, thing, or action you want.
A path that electric charge can move through when the path makes a complete loop.
Movement around a place or along a path that brings something back again.
A large society with a shared way of life and organized systems, often including cities, trade, or government.
The usual pattern of weather in a place over many years.
A curled part of the inner ear that helps change sound vibrations into signals the brain can use.
An icy object that travels around the Sun and can grow glowing tails of gas and dust as it warms up.
To look at two or more things to see how they are alike or different.
The change from a gas to a liquid. It can happen when water vapor touches something cooler.
Something that has to be true for a rule or action to apply.
A material that lets electricity or heat move through it easily.
The basic rules that describe how a government is organized and what it can do. A constitution can also protect people’s rights.
One of the largest land areas into which people divide Earth. Different maps sometimes group them in different ways.
A small ocean animal with a soft, tube-shaped body. Many corals live in groups and make hard structures that can build up into reefs.
Growing different kinds of crops on the same land in a planned order, often to keep soil healthy and reduce pests.
Wanting to know or find out about something.
The kind of money used in a country or shared by several countries.
A flow of water or air in a particular direction.
A hoofed animal with long legs. In many kinds, the males grow pointed, branching antlers each year.
An area of land built from sand, mud, or other material dropped by a river near its mouth.
The bottom number in a fraction, showing how many equal parts make one whole.
How much matter is packed into a given amount of space. A small block of metal is usually denser than a wooden block of the same size.
A way a group of people uses a language. It can have its own sounds, words, and ways of putting words together.
The broad muscle below your lungs that helps you breathe.
The way your body breaks food down into small parts it can take in and use.
To act, work on a task, or carry it out.
To make a picture, shape, or line by marking a surface.
To control a ball while moving, such as by bouncing it in basketball or with small kicks in soccer.
To take a liquid into your mouth and swallow it.
To control the movement of a car, truck, or other vehicle.
An object that orbits the Sun, is nearly round, and shares its neighborhood with other objects of similar importance. It is not a moon.
A thin layer of tissue in the ear that moves when sound reaches it.
A shaking of the ground that usually happens when rocks suddenly slip past one another deep below the surface.
To take food into your mouth and swallow it, usually after chewing.
Finding where things are by making sounds and listening for the echoes that bounce back.
An event in space when one object blocks another from view or moves into its shadow.
The living things in a place, the nonliving things around them, and the ways they affect one another.
A basic chemical substance made of just one kind of atom, such as gold or oxygen.
Something that can be passed or stored and that makes changes possible, such as moving things, heating them, or making light.
An imaginary line all the way around Earth halfway between the North Pole and South Pole.
Equal in value or meaning, even if shown in a different way.
The wearing away and carrying off of soil or pieces of rock by moving water, wind, or ice, or by gravity.
The tube that carries swallowed food and drinks from the throat to the stomach.
To use clues to make a reasonable guess about a number, amount, or size.
A partly sheltered area near the coast where fresh water from land often mixes with salt water from the sea.
The change from liquid to gas that happens at a liquid’s surface.
Facts, objects, or observations that help you check whether an idea is true.
Change in the traits that living things pass to their young over many generations.
To move downward or drop, usually because of gravity.
A way of organizing a country so that power is divided between a national government and governments for smaller parts, such as states.
Something that lets some parts of a mixture through and holds other parts back.
A fine powder made by grinding grain, beans, or similar foods. People use it in bread and many other foods.
The part of some plants that helps them make seeds. It often has colorful petals.
To move through the air, with wings, in an aircraft, or in another way.
The part of a person’s or animal’s body at the end of a leg that touches the ground when standing or walking.
A push or pull that can change how something moves or change its shape.
To stop remembering something or fail to think of it when you need it.
A part, shape, or trace of a living thing from long ago that was preserved naturally.
A way to name a number by telling how many equal parts of a whole you have.
Easy to break or damage, so it needs careful handling.
To change from a liquid to a solid because of cold, or make that happen.
The point that a lever turns around.
An enormous group of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity.
A kind of matter that spreads out to fill the space around it. Air is a mixture of several gases.
To pass something to someone so they can use it, keep it, or have it for a while.
A huge mass of ice that forms on land as layers of snow pile up and squeeze together. It moves slowly under its own weight.
To move or travel from one place to another.
A large waterbird with a long neck and feet that help it paddle.
The attraction between things that have mass. It pulls objects toward Earth and holds planets in their paths around the Sun.
To get bigger or develop over time, or to make a plant develop by taking care of it.
To keep trying or wait patiently when something is hard or slow.
To notice sounds with your ears.
One half of a ball-shaped object, especially one half of Earth.
In or to the place where you are or where you are pointing.
To put yourself or something else where it cannot easily be seen or found.
One sign in a writing system that uses picture-like shapes to stand for sounds, words, or ideas. Ancient Egyptians used such signs.
To begin studying, especially with care and effort.
To have something in your hand, arms, or another secure place.
An opening through a thing, or a space that goes into a surface.
One of two or more words that sound the same but have different meanings, such as sea and see.
A group of words that means something different as a group from what the separate words might suggest.
Words or signs written, stamped, or cut onto a surface, such as stone, metal, or paper.
A long, folded tube in the body that helps take useful parts from food and carry along the rest.
Bringing water to land or plants with pipes, channels, or other equipment, especially when rain alone is not enough.
To watch someone or something and be ready to notice a change or problem.
One of the body parts that clean the blood and make urine from some waste and extra water.
In earlier times in parts of Europe, a trained warrior who often rode a horse and served a ruler. In some places today, knighthood is a special honor.
To have learned or understood something so that you can remember or use it.
A measure in degrees of how far north or south a place is from the equator.
Melted rock that reaches Earth’s surface, or the rock it makes after cooling.
To guide people or animals by showing them where to go or what to do.
To go away from a place or person.
The group of people responsible for making laws for a country, state, or other area.
A stiff bar that turns around a point and helps move something.
A place or service where people can read, borrow, or use shared books and other materials.
A kind of energy that lets our eyes see things when it reaches them.
Something that connects two things, such as a ring in a chain or an item on a page that opens another page.
A kind of matter that flows and takes the shape of the part of a container it fills.
Something being carried, lifted, or supported.
A measure in degrees of how far east or west a place is from a line called the prime meridian.
To stop having something or be unable to find it.
Hot, partly or fully melted rock beneath Earth’s surface.
An object that can attract certain metals, such as iron, and pull or push other magnets without touching them.
To create or put something together.
To come together with someone, whether you planned it or not. It can also mean being introduced for the first time.
A solid material that forms in nature and has its own chemical makeup and a regular pattern inside.
Wrongly or in a way that makes a mistake.
A group of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds.
A natural object that travels around a planet, dwarf planet, or other small world. We call Earth’s own moon the Moon.
A picture or pattern made by fitting together many small pieces of stone, tile, glass, or another material.
A small animal with sharp front teeth for gnawing, rounded ears, and usually a long tail.
A place or organization that collects, cares for, and shows objects or works so people can learn about them.
A tiny part of a kidney that filters the blood, then takes useful material back.
A nerve cell that carries a message in the body.
The part of each day between evening and morning when the Sun is below the horizon.
A way to write down information with a set of signs or symbols.
A line with marked spots showing where numbers are in order and how far apart they are.
The top number in a fraction, showing how many of the equal-size parts are counted.
A substance that a living thing needs to grow, get energy, or stay healthy.
To look at or notice something carefully, often to learn about it.
Still deciding between two choices or opinions.
Understanding a situation in the same way or agreeing on what to do.
Very seldom or hardly ever.
The path an object follows as it travels around another object in space.
A group of musicians who play different instruments together, often led by a conductor.
A gas in air that your body needs, carried from the lungs by blood.
Two things, people, or animals that go together or are used together.
A secret you enter to help prove that you are allowed to use something.
A tool that stores and helps you use your passwords safely.
A fruit that is usually narrow near the stem and rounder at the other end.
A piece of land with water on most sides and a connection to a larger piece of land.
The distance all the way around the edge of a flat shape.
A single human being.
The title for the men and women who ruled ancient Egypt. A ruler with this title is also called a pharaoh.
A trick where someone sends a message that looks real to get private information or get someone to do something unsafe.
A way that plants and some other living things use light energy to make sugars. Most plants use water and carbon dioxide to do this.
Something so easy it takes little effort.
How high or low a sound seems.
A large, nearly round object in space that travels around a star or the remains of a star. Planets in our solar system have cleared most other objects from their paths.
The tiny grains that seed plants make and move by wind, animals, or other means. The grains carry cells that help the plant make seeds.
The moving of pollen to a part of a plant that can receive it, a step that can help the plant make seeds.
An animal that carries pollen so it can reach the part of a plant that receives it.
A picture made to show a person, often their face.
A broad area of grassland, often with very few trees. The name is used especially for grasslands in central North America.
Before, or earlier than.
Water that falls from clouds as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
To say what you think will happen, often based on patterns or other clues.
A word part added at the beginning of another word or word part that helps change its meaning.
Making art by transferring a design from a surface, like a block or plate, to paper, cloth, or another surface.
A way to show the curved surface of Earth on a flat map. Each way changes some distances, shapes, or sizes.
A wheel with a groove along its edge that guides a rope or cable.
Again, as part of a word for doing something another time.
To work out the meaning of written words or signs, by sight, touch, or another method.
A flat shape with four straight sides and four square corners.
A practice session for a performance, ceremony, or other event.
Able to be trusted to work well, show up, or give information that is usually right.
A person chosen to speak or act for other people.
A country where leaders govern on behalf of the public and the head of the country is not a ruler who gets the job by birth.
A pattern of sounds, beats, or movements as they happen in time.
To travel on or in a vehicle or on the back of an animal.
Correct or suitable for what is needed.
A natural solid material made of one or more minerals or other solid substances.
The turning of something around a center or an axis. The word can also mean one whole turn.
To move quickly on foot, taking quicker steps than when walking.
The watery liquid your mouth makes to moisten food and start breaking it down.
An open area of grass with scattered trees, often in a warm place with a wet season and a dry season.
To speak words or show a message in writing.
A tool that shows how heavy something is.
The salt water that covers much of Earth, or one particular part of that water.
To notice something with your eyes.
A plant part that holds a tiny young plant and can grow into a new plant in the right conditions.
A place or collection that stores seeds to preserve different plants for the future.
To cause a thing, message, or person to go to another place.
An animal related to a goat, often raised for its wool, milk, or meat.
To give off light or look bright as light bounces off something.
To let someone see something, or help them see how to do it.
A sign or message that tells what is happening or what to do.
To make music with your voice by moving among notes.
To rest your body on your bottom with the upper part of your body usually upright.
A muscle that can help move your body by pulling on a bone.
To be in the natural resting state in which you are less aware of things around you and may dream.
The Sun and the objects held near it by gravity, including planets, moons, comets, and asteroids. Systems around other stars are often called planetary systems.
A kind of matter that keeps its own shape under ordinary conditions.
Vibrations that travel through material such as air, water, or a wall and can often be heard.
To use your voice to say words. It can also mean being able to use a language.
A group of living things of the same kind. Members of many species can have young with one another, though scientists also use other clues to tell species apart.
A thick bundle of nerve tissue protected by the backbone that carries many messages between the brain and body.
To stay upright on your feet.
A huge ball of hot gas in space that gives off its own light. The Sun is the nearest one to Earth.
The part of your body that holds food after you swallow it and mixes it with juices.
Strong and able to stand up to weight, use, or bumps.
A word part added at the end of a word or word part. It can change the meaning or how a word works in a sentence.
The right to vote in an election.
To move through water by moving your body, legs, fins, or arms.
One beat or part of a spoken word, usually built around a vowel sound.
The part that sticks out at the back of many animals’ bodies.
To pick up or get something, or carry it with you to another place.
A story about something that happened or could have happened.
To help someone learn a fact, an idea, or a skill.
A large piece of Earth’s stiff outer layer. It moves very slowly compared with the other pieces.
To give someone information or say what happened.
A strong strip of tissue that joins a muscle to a bone or another body part.
To use your mind to consider something, form an idea, or solve a problem.
To send something through the air by swinging your arm and letting it go.
A regular rise and fall of the ocean’s water level caused mostly by the pull of the Moon’s gravity. The Sun’s gravity also affects it.
One of the hard parts in the mouth that help you bite and chew food.
To give something to someone and receive something else in return.
A formal agreement between countries or other governments.
A muscle at the back of your upper arm that helps straighten your elbow.
Not, or the opposite of. It can describe someone or something that lacks a quality.
Feeling a little sick or unwell.
To know what something means, how it works, or why it happened.
The liquid waste you pass when you pee.
A part that opens or closes to control where liquid or gas moves.
An official refusal to approve a plan or proposed law, or the power to refuse that approval.
A quick back-and-forth or up-and-down movement that repeats.
An opening in Earth’s surface through which hot rock, ash, and gas can escape. The word can also mean the mountain that builds up around the opening.
In games such as tennis or soccer, a hit or kick made before the ball touches the ground.
The ongoing movement of Earth’s water among air, land, the ground below us, and rivers, lakes, and oceans.
An area of land where streams and runoff all drain toward the same river, lake, or other place.
A repeating movement, or a single traveling bump, that carries energy from one place to another.
A path or direction you can take to reach a place.
To have clothing, jewelry, or something else on your body.
What the air and sky are like in a place at a particular time, including heat, rain, clouds, and wind.
To find out how heavy something is, or to be a certain weight.
A word used when showing two or more choices, or when saying that something is uncertain.
Including all the parts, or still in one piece.
To finish in first place or do better than the other side in a contest. It can also mean getting a prize through effort or luck.
The main tube that carries air from your throat toward your lungs.
To make letters, words, or symbols so someone can read them later.
